The model lifecycle pipeline ensures robustness through structured training and evaluation, while equivariant architecture design leverages symmetry principles to generalize across data transformations. Finally, the planning algorithm framework enables intelligent agent behavior by combining learned models with symbolic reasoning. These components interact through shared abstraction layers—data invariants, policy representations, and temporal logic—that allow for compositional reasoning and modular extension. Dualities emerge in how symmetry constraints shape both model capacity and planning efficiency. Failure modes arise from misalignment between these layers, such as when symmetry assumptions break down during deployment or when planning algorithms cannot handle complex learned reward surfaces.
